inputs.original_text: Activists in Uttar Pradesh are rightly calling out the government's failure to create any workable process for brick kiln operators to get environmental clearances, even three months after the mandate was supposed to take effect. This isn't a simple delay—it's yet another example of how broken institutions protect the powerful while leaving vulnerable communities exposed to ongoing environmental harm and inequality. Brick kiln owners already have State Pollution Control Board approvals for water and air standards and say they're ready to comply if the system gets cleaned up and freed from middlemen interference rooted in systemic corruption and power imbalances. Legal experts are pushing for the state to follow through on court decisions and build an actual approval framework, and this matters deeply for advancing the structural reforms we need to stop sacrificing marginalized groups to profit-driven inaction.
inputs.modified_text: Activists in Uttar Pradesh are correctly highlighting the government's failure to establish any workable process for brick kiln operators to obtain environmental clearances, even three months after the mandate was supposed to take effect. This is not a minor bureaucratic issue but a clear sign of how institutions are built to shield the powerful and wealthy, while exposing vulnerable communities to ongoing environmental harm and deepening inequality rooted in historical power imbalances. Brick kiln owners already hold State Pollution Control Board approvals for water and air standards and state they are ready to comply if the process is fixed and cleared of middlemen interference tied to systemic corruption. Legal experts are pushing for the state to implement court decisions and create a real approval framework. This situation demands urgent structural reforms to protect marginalized groups from being sacrificed to profit-driven inaction.
